rejected.title: Blood Smear Wright-Giemsa Stain
rejected.description: A blood smear—also known as a peripheral blood smear or blood film—is a thin layer of blood spread onto a glass microscope slide and stained to enable microscopic examination of the different blood cells. Blood smears are used in the evaluation of hematological disorders and are routinely performed to detect blood parasites, including those that cause malaria and filariasis. Wright’s stain is a hematologic stain used to distinguish different types of blood cells. It traditionally consists of a mixture of eosin (red) and methylene blue dyes. The stain is primarily applied to peripheral blood smears, urine samples, and bone marrow aspirates for examination under a light microscope. In cytogenetics, Wright’s stain is also used to stain chromosomes, aiding in the diagnosis of various syndromes and diseases.
